what: CO2 in the FLASH3 liquid (stream 24, 30 C, 69.25 bar): the paper's Aspen simulation, CHEPTA, and measured solubility

xia_2004.source: Xia et al. 2004, doi 10.1021/je049803i, ThermoML data set 1 (measured); mole fractions converted by Lab (derived)
xia_2004.note: Gas phase CO2 with the solvent's own vapour (no H2, N2); total pressure is used for the CO2 partial pressure, which overstates it by the solvent vapour (about 20 kPa at 313.75 K, Raoult estimate, assumed), so the interpolated x_CO2 is slightly low. 313.75 K is 10.6 K above the separator's 303.15 K: solubility rises as temperature falls.

bezanehtak_2004.source: Bezanehtak et al. 2004, doi 10.1021/je0301491, ThermoML data set 2 (measured)
bezanehtak_2004.selection: vapour H2 0.68-0.76, 4-7 MPa (the separator: H2 0.73 in the gas, 6.9 MPa)
bezanehtak_2004.note: Pure methanol as solvent: more CO2 dissolves than in 1:1 methanol + water (Xia 2004 at 313.75 K: pure methanol about 3.5 times the 1:1 solvent at the same pressure), so these are upper bounds for stream 24.

xie_2005.source: Xie et al. 2005, doi 10.1021/je0498614, ThermoML data set 1 (measured): CO2 + methanol bubble pressures, 313.2 K
xie_2005.note: Pure methanol: an upper bound for the 1:1 solvent.
